plans.name: Pay per running second
plans.note: No published subscription fee or concurrency guarantee; current offers vary.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv 4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.
GPU prices are live from-offers and changed between search cache and render: use renderedA 6000$.68/28 CPU/58 GB andA 100-40 GB $2.69/30 CPU/200 GB, not cached $.77/$1.89.

Whole-node rates include multiple cards; do not multiplyH 200$43.20 by 8 again. Docs initially say checkpointing only one card, while offers list multi-card minima:capability/launch conflict requires confirmation.
Default idle timeout is disabled;--ttl minimum 60 seconds is opt-in. Files only persist under /workspace. Warm resumes retain RAM; fork descriptions guarantee baseline disk, not all process memory.
Homepage calculator says $20 ofcredit buys 220 hours; that is not proof of a free $20 signup grant. Network pricing, concurrency andsnapshot retention unverified.

Desktop: llms.txt documents an optional virtual desktop (`tama new --desktop`, "these machines resume cold"; SDK tama.desktop() returns a browser desktop URL) and a browser terminal. No managed browser/CDP endpoint or computer-use (screenshot/click) API is documented, so browser and computer_use are false.
Egress and extra-disk prices: still not published (llms.txt / docs / offers API re-checked 2026-09-28; /workspace is a fixed durable 50 GiB disk, no resize price). Left null.

Live offers drift: on 2026-09-28 the offers API briefly showed H100 $3.375/h and L40S $2.295/h; on 2026-09-29 it is back to H100 $3.6855 and L40S $1.188 (= card). H200/B200/Gaudi 2 are still absent from the live API and live rate card (only in the site's static fallback catalogue). A16 (2-card box $1.377/h) and V100/V100-32 ($3.159/h) are live offers, not discontinued.

GPU machines are one card each: '--gpu-count' >1 fails at create because checkpointing more than one card is unsupported. Multi-card nodes (A16 2-card box $1.377/h) are billed whole. Whole-node rentals are 'billed whole for as long as your machine holds it' and may need 'minutes' to provision; serverless-pool cards are per card-hour on shared capacity. --capacity auto|serverless|on-demand exists but the offers API returns one price per card.

Offers API 2026-09-29: RTX4090 and RTX5090 rows have available_nodes 0 and node size 0 (probably serverless-pool cards with no warm workers, not sold out); an A10G row exists with hourly_micros 0 and cards_on_node 0 (placeholder, not orderable). llms.txt also names B200, H200, T4, GH200, B300 as cards, but 'tama offers is the list that is true today' and none of these are in it.
StarSling's 2026-09-29 benchmark run detected an OCI container (not a VM) inside this provider's 4 vCPU / 8 GB sandbox; the card keeps the provider's documented isolation (vm) until confirmed.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote:
a stopped machine is billed for
nothing, and stopping snapshots it on the way down.
snapshot_auto.note: Triggers: every stop (API/CLI/dashboard) unless --no-snapshot, and the opt-in idle policy (--ttl / auto_stop_seconds, min 60 s, disabled by default: 'Tama snapshots and uses the ordinary stop path when the deadline expires'). Memory included ('warm') for normal machines: 'A warm restore comes back in about a second with the processes that were running still running, GPU memory and CUDA context included.' Machines created with --desktop capture disk only (cold). Also automatic crash-recovery snapshots ('snapshot list --all: Include the ones taken automatically to recover from a crash'). Start restores automatically.

snapshot_on_demand.note: tama snapshot create / tama.snapshots.create(machine, label) on a running machine; snapshot list shows RESTORES 'memory+disk' or 'disk'. New machines boot from it: tama fork <snapshot|machine> and templates (private or public). But 'Memory checkpoints belong to stop and start on one machine; a fork or template launch always boots the exact filesystem cold.' So memory is kept only for restoring the same machine; forks/templates are disk-only (template has_memory flag exists for same-workspace launches per llms.txt).

harness_api.quote: A thin launcher starts the existing Claude or Codex CLI inside the machine; tama does not replace either provider's harness, tools, instructions or subagents. The server owns a machine-scoped AgentSession and copies stdout and stderr into its durable transcript.
harness_api.note: Harnesses: Claude Code and Codex (both in base image). CLI tama prompt / SDK prompt(name, prompt, agent='claude'|'codex', detach=True) returns a session id; tama logs <session> replays/follows the durable transcript; tama.sessions.list(machine) lists sessions; dashboard Agents tab. No documented follow-up/resume-conversation call (each prompt is a new headless run); stream is raw stdout/stderr, not structured events.

ingress_rules.quote: The URL is the credential. Its hostname starts with a forty-character random machine token and ends with the port, so it will not be guessed and stays unique across workspaces. Anyone you send it to can reach the port. Treat it as a shared secret rather than as an address, and use tama port-forward when it should not leave your machine.
ingress_rules.note: Only ports you publish (tama expose/unexpose, --port) get a public unguessable HTTPS URL; no auth/IP allowlist on published URLs. Private alternative: tama port-forward over the authenticated tunnel. 'There is no SSH port open to the internet' (SSH via ProxyCommand tama tunnel). Ports 2222/7681/8080 reserved. Weak control (bearer-URL), but per-port choice + private forwarding.

secret_proxy.quote: Inject a workspace secret as that environment variable
secret_proxy.note: Workspace secrets are write-only in the API but are injected as env vars into the machine / agent process ('the encrypted runtime store, which injects it only into that agent process'); they are not in snapshots/forks/templates, but the sandboxed process sees the real value. No credential-injecting proxy.

anti_bot.quote: Give your agent a machine to hack on and pay by the second. Use it for coding agents, kernel development, or inference optimization.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (a general-purpose Linux VM/GPU compute product, not a browser-automation/scraping product; no stealth or fingerprinting feature is documented)

captcha_solving.quote: Give your agent a machine to hack on and pay by the second. Use it for coding agents, kernel development, or inference optimization.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (compute/GPU VM product with no browser/CAPTCHA feature documented)

wake_on_request.quote: Auto-stop is disabled by default. Set auto_stop_seconds=900 when creating a machine to snapshot and stop it after 15 minutes without Tama-visible activity.
wake_on_request.note: Stopped machines are restarted only via explicit tama start/machine.start() calls; no documented behavior where an inbound HTTP/SSH request to a stopped machine automatically wakes it.

volume_attach.quote: Work under `/workspace`. It is the durable 50 GiB disk, every shell starts there, and it is the only place edits survive a stop.
volume_attach.note: Only one fixed durable disk (/workspace) is documented; no CLI/SDK command creates, attaches, or detaches additional volumes.

volume_shared.quote: Work under `/workspace`. It is the durable 50 GiB disk, every shell starts there, and it is the only place edits survive a stop.
volume_shared.note: Each machine has its own private disk; forks copy the disk rather than sharing it ('A fork boots cold from a copy of the snapshot's disk ... no attempt inherits anything from another'). No shared-volume feature documented.

live_resize.quote:
--cpu <CORES>  fractional allowed; 1 is the floor
--memory <MIB> MiB, not GiB; 1024 is the floor
live_resize.note: CPU/RAM are set only at machine creation (--cpu/--memory flags); no documented API/CLI call to change resources of a running machine without recreating it.

own_agent_api.quote: A thin launcher starts the existing Claude or Codex CLI inside the machine; tama does not replace either provider's harness, tools, instructions or subagents.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. tama only launches third-party coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex) inside the VM (harness_api); it has no first-party browser/computer-use/research agent of its own.

mcp_server.quote: Every flag, both SDK quickstarts, and the lines each command prints are at https://tama.computer/docs
mcp_server.note: No MCP server is mentioned anywhere in the CLI docs, llms.txt, or Python/TypeScript SDK guides; control surfaces are the CLI and the two SDKs (gRPC/Connect) only.

lang_python.quote: tama exec box python train.py         # streams output, exits with its code
lang_python.note: Base image ships Python (used directly in worked tasks: pip install, python train.py, pytest -q) as well as Node/npm.

public_ipv4.quote: There is no SSH port open to the internet. The generated config sets ProxyCommand to tama tunnel, so the connection is carried over the same authenticated channel as everything else and port 2222 stays inside the machine.
public_ipv4.note: Inbound reachability is only via provider-generated HTTPS URLs for explicitly exposed ports (tama expose) or the authenticated tunnel/port-forward; no raw public IPv4 address is assigned to or exposed for a machine.

egress_allowlist.quote: Every flag, both SDK quickstarts, and the lines each command prints are at https://tama.computer/docs
egress_allowlist.note: not documented: no outbound allow/deny-list, no-internet mode, or security-group egress control is described anywhere in the CLI/SDK docs.

egress_http_rules.quote: Every flag, both SDK quickstarts, and the lines each command prints are at https://tama.computer/docs
egress_http_rules.note: not documented: no method/path-level egress control is described anywhere in the CLI/SDK docs.

guest_firewall.quote: A machine is a Linux VM you can SSH into, run an agent inside, snapshot mid-task, fork and stop.
guest_firewall.note: derived: full Linux VM with Docker support inside (docker_inside=true) implies guest-side nftables/iptables usage is possible; not separately documented.

windows.quote: A machine is a Linux VM you can SSH into, run an agent inside, snapshot mid-task, fork and stop.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (only Linux/Ubuntu machines are described; no Windows image or flag exists)

macos.quote: A machine is a Linux VM you can SSH into, run an agent inside, snapshot mid-task, fork and stop.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (only Linux/Ubuntu machines are described; no macOS/Apple-silicon VM offering exists)

arm64.quote: Cards include B200, H200, H100, A100-80, RTXPro6000, L40S, RTX5090, A6000, RTX4090, and others such as T4, L4, A10G, V100, GH200 and B300.
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. All documented machine/card options are x86 (Ubuntu base image, NVIDIA GPU nodes); no ARM/aarch64 CPU option is mentioned.

self_host.quote: `--api` and `--console` point the CLI somewhere other than production, and fall back to `TAMA_API` and `TAMA_CONSOLE`.
self_host.note: tama is a hosted SaaS control plane/gateway (production API/console); no self-hosting instructions or on-prem deployment option are documented.

byoc.quote: `--api` and `--console` point the CLI somewhere other than production, and fall back to `TAMA_API` and `TAMA_CONSOLE`.
byoc.note: No bring-your-own-cloud/deploy-into-your-account option is documented; the service runs machines on tama's own infrastructure via its production gateway.

open_source.note: No public GitHub org/source repository for the core tama service was found; the Python/TypeScript packages are client SDKs, not the core sandbox product, and no OSI license is claimed for the platform itself.

soc2.quote: URL: https://tama.computer/security STATUS: 200 (redirects to the homepage; no dedicated security/trust content page exists)
soc2.note: not offered: no security/compliance/trust page or SOC 2 mention exists on the site or in docs.

hipaa.quote: URL: https://tama.computer/trust STATUS: 200 (redirects to the homepage; no dedicated trust/compliance content page exists)
hipaa.note: not offered: no HIPAA/BAA mention exists anywhere on the site or in docs.

sso.quote: `tama login` opens a browser, writes the credential to `~/.tama/config.yaml`, and generates an SSH key and config of its own.
sso.note: Only a single browser-based login / API token flow is documented; no SAML/OIDC SSO feature is mentioned.

eu_data_residency.quote: `--api` and `--console` point the CLI somewhere other than production, and fall back to `TAMA_API` and `TAMA_CONSOLE`.
eu_data_residency.note: No region/location selection flag or EU-residency option is documented anywhere (card's own `regions` field is also null); machine placement/region is not exposed to users.

max_session_h.quote: You are billed for the seconds a machine is running; a stopped machine is billed for nothing, and stopping snapshots it on the way down.
max_session_h.note: A machine (VM) runs until explicitly stopped/rm'd or until an opt-in idle auto-stop (--ttl, disabled by default) fires; no maximum wall-clock session length is imposed.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: A fork boots cold from a copy of the snapshot's disk, which is what makes attempts comparable: no attempt inherits anything from another, and neither can write over the other.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Docs explicitly say fork is disk-only/cold; memory ('warm', with running processes/GPU context) is only restored via stop+start on the SAME machine, not carried into a fork. Confirms false.

browser.quote:
tama.desktop(name_or_id)              # browser desktop URL
    tama.terminal(name_or_id)             # browser terminal URL
browser.note: The only browser-related surfaces are a browser-viewable virtual desktop (`--desktop`, VNC-style stream) and a browser-viewable SSH terminal — both are the human viewing a remote UI over HTTP, not a managed/automatable browser instance. No headless browser, CDP endpoint, or browser-as-a-service is documented anywhere in llms.txt or /docs. Confirms false.

computer_use.quote: `--desktop`             include the virtual desktop; these machines resume cold
computer_use.note: The `--desktop` flag adds a VNC-like virtual desktop reachable via a browser URL (tama.desktop()), but there is no documented API to drive it programmatically by screenshots/clicks (no screenshot/click/type endpoints in the CLI, Python SDK, TypeScript SDK, or docs). desktop=true is correct (graphical desktop exists) but computer_use (screenshot+click driving API) is not offered. Confirms false.

egress_ip_type.quote: Give your agent a machine to hack on and pay by the second. Use it for coding agents, kernel development, or inference optimization.
egress_ip_type.note: derived: tama is a general-purpose Linux VM/GPU compute provider (not a proxy/scraping/residential-IP product); no residential, mobile, or ISP-IP feature is documented anywhere in llms.txt, /docs, or the offers API, so outbound traffic is treated as ordinary datacenter IP space typical of this class of provider.

static_egress_ip.quote: There is no SSH port open to the internet. The generated config sets ProxyCommand to tama tunnel, so the connection is carried over the same authenticated channel as everything else and port 2222 stays inside the machine.
static_egress_ip.note: No IP-address feature of any kind (public IPv4, fixed/static outbound IP, purchasable IPv4) is mentioned anywhere in llms.txt, /docs, or the pricing page; the network section of the card (ipv4_available, ipv4_month) is also null/unpublished. No fixed outbound IP option is documented.

usage_api.quote: Complete Tama surface: tama.usage(days=30) # balance and metered usage
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: yes; The tama.usage(days=30) method in Python SDK and await tama.usage(30) in TypeScript SDK returns balance and metered usage, but only at the account level with a days parameter. There is no documented way to query usage for a specific machine/sandbox by ID, name, tag, label, or project. The method signature does not accept a machine identifier, making it account-only usage reporting rather than per-sandbox or per-group usage.

locations_quote: No region/location selection flag or EU-residency option is documented; machine placement/region is not exposed to users.
